steps.title: Prepare Triton‑X‑100/ammonium hydroxide solution
steps.instruction: Mix 10 mL of 1 % Triton X‑100, 4 mL of 25 % ammonium hydroxide (final 0.004 %), and 986 mL double‑distilled water (DDW) to a total volume of 1 L.

steps.title: Prepare Triton‑X‑100/EDTA/Tris solution
steps.instruction: Combine 10 mL of 1 % Triton X‑100, 2.6 g EDTA powder (final 0.26 %), 6.9 g Tris base (final 0.69 %), and DDW to a final volume of 1 L.

steps.title: Prepare peracetic acid/ethanol solution
steps.instruction: Add 1 mL glacial acetic acid, 1 mL 33 % H₂O₂, 40 mL absolute ethanol, and 958 mL DDW; mix to obtain 0.4 % peracetic acid / 4 % ethanol solution (1 L total).

steps.title: Prepare pepsin digestion solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 5 mg pepsin powder in 5 mL 0.01 M HCl to give 1 mg mL⁻¹ pepsin solution (scale proportionally for other tissue amounts).

steps.title: Prepare DNase I solution (50 U mL⁻¹)
steps.instruction: Weigh 0.071 mg DNase I powder (3 520 U mg⁻¹) and dissolve in 5 mL 1× PBS.

steps.title: Prepare 70 % ethanol
steps.instruction: Mix 350 mL absolute ethanol with 150 mL DDW.

steps.title: Prepare 3 % hydrogen peroxide solution
steps.instruction: Combine 45.5 mL 33 % H₂O₂ with 454.5 mL DDW.

steps.title: Euthanize mice (IACUC)
steps.instruction: Sacrifice mice according to institutional animal care and use committee guidelines.

steps.title: Cardiac perfusion
steps.instruction: Insert a butterfly needle into the left ventricle, cut the right ventricle, and perfuse with DDW using a 20 mL syringe at low‑to‑medium pressure.

steps.title: Initial DDW soak of tissue
steps.instruction: Place lungs or tumor in 50 mL DDW in a 50 mL conical tube; rotate 2 h at 4 °C, 30 rpm.

steps.title: Extended DDW wash
steps.instruction: Replace DDW and rotate at least 48 h at 4 °C, 30 rpm, changing the DDW once every 24 h until the tissue no longer appears reddish.

steps.title: Triton‑X‑100/ammonium hydroxide treatment
steps.instruction: Exchange DDW for 50 mL Triton X‑100/ammonium hydroxide solution; rotate 48 h at 4 °C, 30 rpm. If tissue is not clear, replace with fresh solution and continue 24 h more.

steps.title: DDW washes post‑detergent
steps.instruction: Wash tissue three times with DDW, 15 min each, on a horizontal shaker at room temperature (RT), 300 rpm.

steps.title: Fat removal (tumor only)
steps.instruction: At RT, rotate tissue in 50 mL 70 % ethanol for 12 h; then 15 min in 50 mL 3 % H₂O₂; then 2 h in 50 mL 0.4 % peracetic acid/4 % ethanol; finish with three 15‑min DDW washes on shaker RT, 300 rpm.

steps.title: DNase I digestion
steps.instruction: Incubate tissue in 5 mL DNase I solution (50 U mL⁻¹) while rotating at 150 rpm, 37 °C for 1 h.

steps.title: First DDW wash after DNase
steps.instruction: Wash with DDW for 2 h on an Intelli‑Mixer at 4 °C, 30 rpm.

steps.title: Second DDW wash (24 h)
steps.instruction: Replace DDW with fresh DDW and wash for 24 h at 4 °C, 30 rpm.

steps.title: PBS addition and tissue mincing
steps.instruction: Transfer decellularized tissue to a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube, add 200 µL 1× PBS, cut into small pieces with scissors.

steps.title: Centrifugation and storage
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 2 min, discard supernatant, and store tissue at –80 °C (up to 1 year).

steps.title: Euthanize mice for skin (IACUC)
steps.instruction: Sacrifice mice according to IACUC guidelines.

steps.title: Cardiac perfusion for skin
steps.instruction: Perform cardiac perfusion as described above, flowing DDW through a 20 mL syringe at low‑to‑medium pressure.

steps.title: Skin depilation
steps.instruction: Shave desired skin area and apply depilatory cream for 1–2 min.

steps.title: Skin collection and subcutaneous removal
steps.instruction: Collect skin, separate from underlying tissues, manually remove subcutaneous layer with a scalpel.

steps.title: Skin sectioning and storage
steps.instruction: Cut skin into 1 cm² rectangles, place each in a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube, and store at –80 °C (up to 1 year).

steps.title: Sequential skin decellularization
steps.instruction: Place 1–2 skin sections in a 50 mL tube and incubate on a horizontal shaker (300 rpm, RT unless noted) in the following solutions:

substeps.instruction: 0.25 % Trypsin‑EDTA (0.038 %) in HBSS: 6 h at 37 °C, 300 rpm.
1 % Triton X‑100/0.26 % EDTA/0.69 % Tris: 6 h (once) then overnight incubation.
DNase I solution (50 U mL⁻¹): 1 h at 37 °C, 300 rpm.
DDW: three washes, 15 min each, then overnight incubation.

steps.title: PBS addition and mincing (skin)
steps.instruction: Transfer decellularized skin to a 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube, add 200 µL PBS, and cut into small pieces with scissors.

steps.title: Centrifugation and storage (skin)
steps.instruction: Centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 2 min, discard supernatant, and store at –80 °C (up to 1 year).

steps.title: Punch Eppendorf tube cups
steps.instruction: Using a 27 G needle, make 7–10 holes in the cap of an Eppendorf tube, cut out the punched cup, and place it on the tissue‑containing tube.

steps.title: Lyophilize tissues
steps.instruction: Freeze‑dry at –110 °C: 24 h for tumors and lungs, 48 h for skin; then close the tubes with the original caps.

steps.title: Store lyophilized samples
steps.instruction: Keep lyophilized tubes at –80 °C (several months).

steps.title: Weigh lyophilized tissue
steps.instruction: Record the dry weight of each sample before grinding.

steps.title: Grind tissue with pepsin
steps.instruction: Add 200 µL pepsin solution to the tube, grind with a handheld tissue grinder until homogeneous; add more pepsin solution if needed and note the total volume used.

steps.title: Adjust tissue‑to‑pepsin ratio
steps.instruction: Transfer the ground material to a scintillation vial; ensure a final ratio of 10 mg lyophilized tissue per 1 mL pepsin solution, adding pepsin solution if necessary.

steps.title: Pepsin digestion incubation
steps.instruction: Incubate on a horizontal shaker at 150 rpm, RT for 24 h (skin) or 48 h (lungs and tumors).

steps.title: Neutralize digestion pH
steps.instruction: Titrate the digested solution to pH 7.2–7.4 with 0.1 M NaOH, adding dropwise and recording the volume added; avoid exceeding pH 7.5.

steps.title: Add 10× PBS
steps.instruction: Add sterile 10× PBS equal to one‑ninth of the total solution volume.

steps.title: Adjust final ECM concentration
steps.instruction: Add sterile 1× PBS to reach a protein concentration of approximately 8–10 mg mL⁻¹.

steps.title: Optional clarification
steps.instruction: If debris is visible, transfer the solution to a new 1.7 mL Eppendorf tube, centrifuge at 11 000 × g for 2 min, and collect the clear supernatant.

steps.title: Store pre‑gel solution
steps.instruction: Keep the pre‑gel at 4 °C for up to 1 week before use.

steps.title: Gel formation
steps.instruction: Aliquot the pre‑gel into the desired platform (e.g., 30–60 µL per well of a 96‑well plate) and incubate at 37 °C for 1 h to allow self‑assembly into a hydrogel.

substeps.instruction: 96‑well plate: 30–60 µL per well (≈0.5–1 mm thickness).
In vivo injection (mouse): 100–300 µL per site.

description: Validation of protocol The reproducibility and robustness of this protocol were validated through independent preparations of ECM hydrogels derived from murine skin, lung, and melanoma tumors. Each tissue type was processed in at least three independent biological replicates, following identical decellularization, lyophilization, digestion, and polymerization steps. The following validation steps were carried out: (A) An effective decellularization process was confirmed by histological evaluation (H&E staining) showing complete removal of nuclei and cellular material. Representative microscopy images of the different tissues were obtained from three replicates. (B) DNA quantification in decellularized tissue demonstrated a significant reduction in DNA content after the decellularization process. The experiment was carried out in triplicate ( Figure 3 ). (C) Collagen preservation and fibrillar organization after hydrogel formation were verified using Picrosirius Red staining under polarized light, revealing site-specific ECM architectures that remained consistent between preparations. Representative images from three to four replicates are shown ( Figure 4 ).
